question: Should OpenClaw core accept model-elected continuation tools and trusted cross-session/session-lifecycle return plumbing as an opt-in agent runtime feature in this PR?
rationale: The patch is not a narrow bug fix: it adds new model-facing tools, config, persisted state, protocol/internal fields, and trusted session-event flows, so automation cannot decide whether this belongs in core or what security/product boundary maintainers want.

options.title: Sponsor the core feature after exact-head proof
options.body: Keep the PR open, require exact-head accepted-success proof for request_compaction and a final owner review of config, protocol, session-state, and security boundaries before merge.

options.title: Narrow to an RFC or plugin/API seam
options.body: Pause the implementation branch and ask the contributor to split out design/docs or the minimal core extension API needed for an external continuation implementation.

options.title: Decline the core direction
options.body: Close the PR as not planned if maintainers decide self-elected continuation and trusted cross-session enrichment should not live in OpenClaw core.

recommendation.title: Sponsor the core feature after exact-head proof
recommendation.body: Keep the PR open, require exact-head accepted-success proof for request_compaction and a final owner review of config, protocol, session-state, and security boundaries before merge.

likelyOwner.reason: martingarramon is the only visible human reviewer in the PR discussion who already commented on the continuation shape and deferred the default-deny/product boundary to maintainers.
